pull.title: fix(installer): install while MCC runs, around a shim Windows will not release
pull.body:
## The failure

Two real installs, three days apart, same shape:

```
04:06  failed to copy ... Scripts\mcc-claude.exe  -> ~\.local\bin\mcc-claude.exe:
       The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process. (os error 32)

16:30  failed to copy ... Scripts\mcc-desktop.exe -> ~\.local\bin\mcc-desktop.exe:
       The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process. (os error 32)
       My Claude Code install failed: Command failed with exit code 2
       At line:709 char:9   throw "My Claude Code install failed: $installError"
```

## Root cause

Line 709 of the shipped v6.32.0 `install.ps1` is the `throw` inside `Invoke-RenameThenReinstall`'s rollback, so the rename path **did** run and the tool-directory rename **had** succeeded. `mcc-desktop` **is** in `Get-LauncherCommands` — the stale-list hypothesis is refuted. The rename of that one shim was refused, and `Rename-LauncherShimsAside` swallowed the refusal:

```powershell
catch {
    # Leave it: uv will fail on this one shim and we report it as a
    # missing command rather than silently shipping a broken set.
}
```

uv does not fail on *one* shim. It aborts the whole entrypoint pass on the first file it cannot write, writes no receipt, and the rollback then throws.

And Windows really does refuse those renames. Measured on a scratch install with `mcc-server`, the `mcc-desktop` tray and an `mcc-claude` session live: **all three** of their shims were refused, the other 35 moved aside without complaint. uv writes entrypoints in ASCII order, so the first refused shim it reached was `mcc-desktop.exe` — the file in the 16:30 error — and `mcc-claude.exe` in the 04:06 one.

*(Which handle holds the file is not identified; it is not needed. The design no longer assumes the rename can always be done.)*

## What changed

**`scripts/install.ps1`**

- `Get-ManagedShimName` (new) — the shim set is a union of three independent sources: the `^(mcc|fcc)-.*\.exe$` family pattern plus `my-claude-code.exe` / `free-claude-code.exe`, every `install-path` in uv's own `uv-receipt.toml`, and the `Get-LauncherCommands` contract list. A new command cannot be missed by all three. The contract test pinning the list to `pyproject.toml` stays, but the rename no longer depends on it.
- `Rename-LauncherShimsAside` — returns one record per shim including `Renamed = $false` and the OS error, instead of an empty `catch`.
- `Invoke-StagedInstall` (new) — the fallback. Re-runs uv with `UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR` at a fresh staging directory, so uv writes all 38 shims and a complete receipt somewhere nothing can be holding, then places them into the real bin directory one file at a time (rename aside with retries, then copy). A destination that still cannot be replaced keeps the old file — restored if it had already been moved aside — and is returned as "kept", never as a failure.
- `Update-UvReceiptEntrypoint` (new) — repoints the receipt's `install-path` entries at the real bin directory through a temp file and an atomic move.
- `Invoke-RenameThenReinstall` — routes to the staged install when any rename was refused **or** when the direct install failed for any other reason; only a failure of *that* rolls back and throws.
- `Install-FreeClaudeCode` — the plain path (nothing detected as running) now also retries through the rename/staged path when uv fails. Process detection is a name match, and a name match can miss.
- Closing summary lists kept shims by name with "these keep working and will refresh on the next install". Still exits non-zero, and still refuses to print "verified", for a command that is genuinely absent.

**`src/my_claude_code/application/release_updates.py`** — the tray/dashboard updater's detached helper gets the same mechanism: family-wide discovery, refusals recorded, staged fallback, receipt repointed, and a result carrying `kept_shims` as refreshing-next-time rather than as errors.

**Docs** — README install-troubleshooting rows and `docs/USAGE.md` §15 now state that installing while MCC is running is supported, that running sessions keep the old version until restarted, and that a locked shim refreshes on the next install.

## The uv receipt finding

Measured with uv 0.11.21: an install run with `UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR` set records every `install-path` under **that** directory:

```toml
{ name = "mccprobe-claude", install-path = ".../installer-fix2/stage/mccprobe-claude.exe", from = "mccprobe" },
```

Left as written, a later `uv tool uninstall` or `uv tool upgrade` would chase a temp path that no longer exists. Rewriting the receipt was chosen over a second full `uv tool install` pass: it is deterministic, costs no second 87-package install, and cannot hit the same lock again. After the staged path the receipt reads:

```toml
{ name = "fcc-anthropic-oauth-login", install-path = ".../rt/bin/fcc-anthropic-oauth-login.exe", from = "my-claude-code" },
```

The direct rename path was kept as the fast path rather than always staging: it is the behaviour already proven in v6.30.1, it is one uv invocation, and uv writes a correct receipt itself.

## Proof: three launchers running

Scratch `UV_TOOL_DIR` / `UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR`, a `uv.cmd` shim that no-ops only `tool update-shell`, `USERPROFILE` redirected so nothing of the user's is touched. Baseline install of v6.32.0 with nothing running (38 shims, verified), then `mcc-server` (port 8199), the `mcc-desktop` tray and an `mcc-claude` session started from the scratch bin directory, then the published scriptblock form run against v6.33.0 with all three live:

```
=== install while all three are running ===
Could not move mcc-claude.exe aside: The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process.
Could not move mcc-desktop.exe aside: The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process.
Could not move mcc-server.exe aside: The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process.
Installing through a staging directory instead (3 launcher shim(s) could not be moved aside).
+ ...uv.cmd tool install --force --refresh-package my-claude-code --python 3.14.0 'my-claude-code @ file:///...my_claude_code-6.33.0-py3-none-any.whl'

==> Configuring PATH and verifying My Claude Code

My Claude Code 6.33.0 is installed and verified.
New sessions and restarted servers use the new version.
Already-open windows keep running the previous version until they are
closed or restarted.

These launchers were locked and kept the file they had:
  mcc-claude, mcc-desktop, mcc-server
These keep working and will refresh on the next install.

=== verdict ===
installer threw: False
[after] shims=38 leftovers=0
  desktop  pid=2336  STILL ALIVE=True
  server   pid=56288 STILL ALIVE=True
  claude   pid=13772 STILL ALIVE=True
  old server /health: 200
  receipt present: True
  uv tool list:
    my-claude-code v6.33.0
    - fcc-anthropic-oauth-login
  receipt entrypoint sample:
    { name = "fcc-anthropic-oauth-login", install-path = ".../rt/bin/fcc-anthropic-oauth-login.exe", from = "my-claude-code" },
  fresh mcc-server --version: my-claude-code 6.33.0
```

Every command present, receipt written and pointing at the real bin directory, all three processes alive, the old server still answering on its port, and a fresh `mcc-server --version` reporting the **new** version through the **old** shim — the version-agnostic-launcher claim demonstrated rather than asserted. The shim's embedded interpreter path was also read directly and is absolute into the canonical tool directory:

```
#!C:\...\installer-fix2\tools\mccprobe\Scripts\python.exe
```

## Proof: the pathological case

Same three processes running, plus `mcc-rtk.exe` held open with `FileShare.None` — nothing can rename it and nothing can write it:

```
=== holding mcc-rtk.exe with FileShare.None ===
Could not move mcc-claude.exe aside: ...
Could not move mcc-desktop.exe aside: ...
Could not move mcc-rtk.exe aside: ...
Could not move mcc-server.exe aside: ...
Installing through a staging directory instead (4 launcher shim(s) could not be moved aside).

My Claude Code 6.33.0 is installed and verified.

These launchers were locked and kept the file they had:
  mcc-claude, mcc-desktop, mcc-rtk, mcc-server
These keep working and will refresh on the next install.

installer threw: False
[after] shims=38 leftovers=0
  all three STILL ALIVE=True ; old server /health: 200
  fresh mcc-server --version: my-claude-code 6.33.0
```

## Tests

New in `tests/scripts/test_installers.py` (static guards, run everywhere):

- `test_installer_moves_the_whole_shim_family_aside_not_a_hand_written_list`
- `test_installer_records_a_refused_rename_instead_of_swallowing_it`
- `test_installer_stages_the_install_when_a_shim_cannot_be_moved_aside`
- `test_installer_restores_the_old_shim_when_the_new_one_cannot_be_placed`
- `test_installer_rewrites_the_receipt_after_a_staged_install`
- `test_installer_never_fails_on_a_locked_file_without_trying_the_fallback`
- `test_installer_reports_kept_shims_as_refreshing_not_as_failures`
- `test_updater_helper_matches_the_installer_rename_and_staged_fallback`
- `test_updater_helper_script_is_valid_powershell_after_rendering` — the helper is built from an f-string, so a broken escape would otherwise ship silently

New runtime PowerShell tests (Windows only, both `powershell.exe` and `pwsh.exe`):

- `test_shim_rename_reports_a_lock_it_cannot_break` — a real locked `.exe` comes back `Renamed = False`; a `mcc-brandnew.exe` no list mentions is still covered by the family pattern; `unrelated.exe` is left alone
- `test_staged_install_keeps_a_locked_shim_and_repoints_the_receipt` — with `mcc-rtk.exe` held `FileShare.None` by a second process: the unlocked shim takes the new file, the locked one keeps a working launcher, `KEPT:mcc-rtk` is returned, and the receipt no longer points into the staging directory

`_POWERSHELL_HELPER_NAMES` gains `Get-ManagedShimName`, `Invoke-StagedInstall` and `Update-UvReceiptEntrypoint`. `_RENAME_DEPENDENCIES` (the runtime extraction set) gains the same three so the existing rename tests still dot-source a complete script.

Counts: `tests/scripts/` + `tests/contracts/` — **406 passed, 17 skipped** with the 6 known-local failures deselected. Full suite: **15 known local failures** (6 PowerShell installer wheel-checksum-fixture, 8 websearch, `test_catalog_publication…`), unchanged by this branch.

## Residual risks

- **Which handle refuses the rename is not identified.** The design does not depend on it, and the staged fallback covers any holder — but it also means the refusal rate on other machines is unknown.
- **The renamed-aside tool directory can survive as `my-claude-code.old-<stamp>`** while processes still run from it, and `uv tool list` prints `warning: Ignoring malformed tool ...` until the next install sweeps it. Pre-existing since v6.30.1; a leading-dot name was tried and makes uv error harder, so the naming was left alone.
- **A command *added* by the release whose shim is locked would be reported missing and exit non-zero.** That is deliberate — it is genuinely absent — but it is the one case where a locked file still costs a re-run.
- **The staging directory lives under `%TEMP%`** and is removed on both branches; a hard kill mid-install could leave one `mcc-stage-bin-*` directory behind.
- **PowerShell installer tests never run on Linux CI**, so a PS-only regression can ship green; the runtime tests above were executed locally on Windows against both shells.

commit.message:
fix(installer): install while MCC runs, around a shim Windows will not release

Installing with the tray and the server open failed outright and rolled back:
uv could not copy `mcc-desktop.exe` over a file "being used by another
process", and the installer threw from Invoke-RenameThenReinstall's rollback.
The rename path had run and the tool-directory rename had succeeded, and
`mcc-desktop` was in the launcher list -- but Rename-LauncherShimsAside caught
the refused rename and did nothing with it, on the assumption that uv would
fail on that one shim alone. uv does not: it aborts the whole entrypoint pass
on the first file it cannot write and leaves no receipt. Measured on a scratch
install with mcc-server, the mcc-desktop tray and an mcc-claude session live,
all three of their shims were refused while the other 35 moved aside, and uv's
ASCII write order reaches mcc-desktop.exe first -- the exact file in the 16:30
failure, and mcc-claude.exe in the 04:06 one.

The shim set is now a union of the mcc-*/fcc- family pattern, uv's own receipt
and the contract list, so no command can be missed by all three. A refused
rename is reported by name with its OS error instead of swallowed, and routes
to a staged install: uv is re-run with UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR pointed at a fresh
staging directory, where it writes every shim and a complete receipt with
nothing in its way, and the shims are then placed into the real bin directory
one at a time. One stuck file costs that one file. A shim that still cannot be
replaced keeps the file it has -- a uv launcher is a version-agnostic stub that
execs the interpreter inside the canonical tool directory, which now holds the
new install -- and is listed as refreshing on the next install rather than
counted as a failure. uv records install-path under whatever UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR
was set to, so the receipt's entrypoints are rewritten back to the real bin
directory through a temp file and an atomic move.

The direct install keeps the fast path, and now falls back to the staged one
whenever it fails for any reason, including on the branch where nothing looked
like it was running: process detection is a name match and a name match can
miss. The dashboard and tray updater's detached helper gets the same
mechanism, and reports kept_shims the same honest way.

Verified on a scratch tool directory upgrading 6.32.0 to 6.33.0 with a live
mcc-server on 8199, a live tray and a live mcc-claude session: 38 commands
present, receipt written and pointing at the real bin directory, all three
processes still alive, the old server still answering /health, and a fresh
mcc-server --version reporting 6.33.0 through an old shim. Same result with
mcc-rtk.exe held open with FileShare.None, which is named as kept.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AxhmPc42yZ6wMyomxP3Ty6

fix(updater): find the tool directory without running uv on the live server

The staged fallback needs the tool directory to repoint the uv receipt, and
reaching for it with `uv tool dir` ran uv while the server was still alive --
the exact thing the deferred path exists to avoid, and a test that has guarded
it since it was written caught it. sys.executable inside a uv tool environment
is <tool dir>/Scripts/python.exe and uv keeps uv-receipt.toml in that same
directory, so the path is already known for free. Outside a uv tool
environment it resolves to nothing and the helper falls back to the family
pattern and the entry points, which already cover every published command.

The receipt rewrite also writes through [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText with a
BOM-less UTF8Encoding, like the helper's other two write sites, so the
no-BOM guard counts three of them rather than two.
